title: 야한 옷 아니고 예쁜 옷인데  (It's Not Racy, It's Pretty)

segments.t: In Cindy's waiting room, Tak Ye-jin cites KBS broadcast standards against Cindy's sheer outfit — until Cindy puts innocent rookie Seung-chan on the spot and threatens to quit the live broadcast. Listen for the phrases for 'a pretty outfit' and 'step outside'.
KBS 심의 규정상 야한 옷 이거 안 돼.
야한 옷 아니고 예쁜 옷인데.
이거 예쁘지 않아요?
거봐요, 피디님, 예쁘다잖아요.
집에서 뮤직뱅크 엄마랑 본 적 있어요?
본 적은 본 것도 같고.
저 이 프로 안 할게요, 저 그냥 가면 돼요.
진짜 안 되겠네, 다들 나가 있어.
Let's walk through the eight lines of this dressing-room standoff.
KBS 심의 규정상 야한 옷 이거 안 돼.

'Under KBS broadcast rules, a racy outfit like this isn't allowed.' Adding the suffix for 'according to' onto the word for 'regulations' means 'under the rules'. The phrase for 'a racy outfit' pairs the word meaning 'risqué' or 'too revealing' with the word for 'clothes' It comes from this.
야한 옷 아니고 예쁜 옷인데.

'It's not a racy outfit, it's a pretty outfit.' Without blinking, Cindy swaps the word for 'racy' for the word for 'pretty'. Trailing off with a soft contrast ending pushes back smoothly while sounding completely composed This short for that.
이거 예쁘지 않아요?

'Isn't this pretty?' Pointing out Seung-chan by his polka-dot tie, she asks a leading question — adding the negative question ending onto 'pretty' turns it into 'isn't it pretty?', daring him to disagree! Notice the word for.
거봐요, 피디님, 예쁘다잖아요.

'See there, PD, he says it's pretty.' After poor Seung-chan nods, Cindy gloats with an expression meaning 'see, told you so!'. Tacking a reminder ending onto 'pretty' tells Ye-jin: 'you just saw him agree it's pretty!' The word doubles the.
집에서 뮤직뱅크 엄마랑 본 적 있어요?

'Have you ever watched Music Bank at home with your mum?' It opens with the words for 'at home' and 'with mum'. Best of all is the experiential question pattern at the end — put any past-word modifier before it to ask 'have you ever...?' Notice the word for.
본 적은 본 것도 같고.

'As for watching it, I think maybe I have.' Caught between two glares, Seung-chan hedges with a topic-marked phrase for 'as for having seen it' and a tentative ending meaning 'seems like maybe so' — peak rookie survival Korean This literally means that.
저 이 프로 안 할게요, 저 그냥 가면 돼요.

'I won't do this show, I can just leave.' Calling Ye-jin's bluff minutes before air, Cindy says she won't do it, using TV shorthand for 'programme'. The final clause means 'all I have to do is walk out' This short for that.
진짜 안 되겠네, 다들 나가 있어.

'This really won't do, everyone step outside.' Realizing a star won't back down in front of an audience, Ye-jin clears the room with the word for 'everybody' and a command meaning 'go out and wait outside' This short for that. Now let's hear the whole dressing-room clash again at full speed.
KBS 심의 규정상 야한 옷 이거 안 돼.
야한 옷 아니고 예쁜 옷인데.
이거 예쁘지 않아요?
거봐요, 피디님, 예쁘다잖아요.
집에서 뮤직뱅크 엄마랑 본 적 있어요?
본 적은 본 것도 같고.
저 이 프로 안 할게요, 저 그냥 가면 돼요.
진짜 안 되겠네, 다들 나가 있어.
You learned how to ask 'isn't it pretty?', how to ask 'have you ever seen...?', and the command to 'step outside'. Let's see how Ye-jin handles Cindy one-on-one!
다음에 또 만나요!
